release_notes: A profit target or other profit-taking exit no longer fires on a leg whose live price is far from its fair value (more than 50% or 20 points off) or below its intrinsic value. A broker can report a stale price for a contract it won't actually trade; the strategy then thinks it hit its target, the close is rejected, and a loss is booked. Stop-losses are unaffected, and the exit fires normally once the price looks real again.
